div.head: ECf 32 B 2
div.ab: Item qui fugiet a domino uel socio suo pro timiditate belli uel mortis, in conductione heretochi sui, in expeditione nauali uel terrestri, perdat omne quod suum est et suam ipsius uitam; et manus mittat dominus ad terram, quam ei antea dederat. Et si terram hereditariam habeat, ipsa in manus regis transeat.
div.note: Liebermann’s text transcribed from Gesetze I p. 657 (November 2026): read from the page images and checked against the scan’s own text layer, differences settled against the page.

This passage is not part of ECf or ECf retr: it is one of the additions of the London collection (Leges Anglorum s. XIII in. Londoniis collectae), which Liebermann prints across the page as an insertion into ECf retr. 32 (32 A–E, pp. 655–660). The dictionary cites it as “ECf 32 B …”, so it is kept with ECf here.
Liebermann prints the words borrowed from Quadripartitus’ Latin of II Cnut in smaller type; his margin names the source (Quadr. II Cn. 77. 77, 1).

note.seg: Quadr. wird hier in frühester Form gebraucht, die aus einem vorhergehenden Stücke desselben Werkes oben S. 365 ff. als Lond notirt ward
Quadr. is used here in its earliest form, which was noted above, p. 365 ff., as Lond from an earlier piece of the same work

div.ab: Likewise, whoever flees from his lord or his companion out of fear of battle or of death, under the leadership of his heretoch, on an expedition by sea or by land, let him lose all that is his and his own life; and let the lord lay hands on the land which he had given him before. And if he has hereditary land, let it pass into the king's hands.
